mentions.name: SoberStack
mentions.description: A free sobriety app for quitting bad habits that uses a GitHub-style contribution graph to visualize long-term progress instead of resetting a counter to zero after a slip. It tracks urges and stores a personal toolbox reminding the user why they are quitting and what alternative actions to take whenever an urge hits.
mentions.problem: Most sobriety apps reset your counter to zero when you slip, losing sight of overall progress.
mentions.audience: Individuals quitting bad habits, built by the author for personal use
mentions.source_excerpt:
I've been building SoberStack (https://soberstack.app). It's the first side project I've taken on in a few years.

It's a free sobriety app for any bad habits I built for myself. Most sobriety apps reset your counter to zero when you slip, but it uses a Github style contribution graph to show you how far you have come. I also use it to track urges, and store a toolbox that is a reminder if why I am quitting something and what I can do instead every time I have an urge.
